subject: gk
question: The Mathura style of sculpture is distinguished by:

options.text: Indian indigenous themes with some Hellenistic influence
Purely Indian styles with no outside influence

solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian indigenous themes with some Hellenistic influence**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mathura School of Art** flourished during the **Kushana Empire**, primarily between the **1st Century AD** and the **3rd Century AD**. This school developed concurrently with the **Gandhara School** but remained rooted in local traditions. ***Hence, the statement regarding its historical age is correct.***
 
• Unlike the Gandhara school, which was heavily influenced by **Greco-Roman** aesthetics, the **Mathura style** was largely an **indigenous** development that evolved from the earlier **Yaksha** and **Yakshini** figures of the **Maurya** and **Sunga** periods. ***Hence, the statement about its indigenous themes is correct.***
 
• The primary material used in the **Mathura School** was **spotted red sandstone**, sourced from nearby quarries like **Sikri** and **Kankali Tila**. This is a distinguishing feature from the **Grey Schist** used in **Gandhara**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the material used is correct.***
 
• While the school is celebrated for its **Indian** character, it was not entirely isolated; as the **Kushana** rulers controlled both **Mathura** and **Gandhara**, a cross-cultural exchange occurred, leading to **Hellenistic influences** appearing in later Mathura works, such as the treatment of **folds in drapery** and certain **iconographic** elements. ***Hence, the statement about Hellenistic influence is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Themes and Religious Diversity:**
 
 
• The **Mathura School** was unique because it catered to three major religions: **Buddhism**, **Jainism**, and **Hinduism**.
 
• In **Buddhism**, it is credited with creating the first human representations of the **Buddha**, who was previously represented only through symbols like the **Bodhi tree** or **footprints**.
 
• In **Jainism**, the school produced numerous **Ayagapattas** (tablet of homage) and statues of **Tirthankaras** characterized by the **Srivatsa** mark on the chest.
 
• In **Hinduism**, early representations of **Shiva** (in **Lingam** and human form), **Vishnu**, and **Surya** were carved during this period.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Location:**
 
 
• The center of this art form was **Mathura**, situated on the banks of the **Yamuna River** in present-day **Uttar Pradesh**, **India**.
 
• Its location at the junction of major trade routes like the **Uttarapath** facilitated the spread of these sculptures to far-off places like **Sarnath** and **Shravasti**.
 
 
 
• **Physical Characteristics of Sculptures:**
 
 
• Sculptures often displayed **fleshy bodies** with a sense of **voluptuousness**, reflecting **Indian** notions of beauty and vitality (**Prana**).
 
• The **Buddha** figures typically featured a **shaven head** (later curly hair), a **large halo** decorated with geometric patterns, and the **Abhaya Mudra** (gesture of fearlessness).
 
• The drapery was usually **transparent** and clung closely to the body, often covering only the left shoulder (**Ekanshika**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Royal Statuary:** A famous example of the **Mathura School** is the **headless statue of Kanishka**, which shows him in **central Asian** attire—heavy boots and a long coat—demonstrating the **Kushana** identity.
 
• **Evolution into Gupta Art:** The **Mathura School** served as the foundation for the **Golden Age** of **Gupta Art** in the **4th and 5th centuries**. The **Gupta** artists refined the **Mathura** style, adding spiritual depth and more intricate decoration to the **haloes**.
 
• **Key Difference from Gandhara:** While **Gandhara** Buddha looked like **Apollo** (Greco-Roman features, wavy hair, muscular), the **Mathura** Buddha was modeled after the **Indian Yakshas** (smiling face, rounder features).
